subsystems.name: Targeting system
subsystems.role: finds the exact spot in the genome where an epigenetic mark should be added or removed.

subsystems.name: Epigenetic effector
subsystems.role: writes or erases chemical marks on DNA or its packaging proteins, changing gene activity without altering the DNA sequence.

subsystems.name: Environmental switch
subsystems.role: turns the effector on only when a chosen condition occurs, such as heat, drought or a specific day length.

subsystems.name: Delivery vector
subsystems.role: gets the editing machinery into plant cells.

subsystems.name: Regeneration and selection
subsystems.role: grows edited cells into whole fertile plants and picks out the ones that worked.

subsystems.name: Validation toolkit
subsystems.role: confirms the epigenetic mark is in the right place and that the plant's behaviour has changed.

buildSteps.title: Choose a trait and target gene
buildSteps.detail: Pick a gene whose activity level controls a useful trait, such as drought survival or grain nutrient content.

buildSteps.title: Map the regulatory region
buildSteps.detail: Work out which DNA or histone marks will raise or lower that gene's expression.

buildSteps.title: Design the guide RNA
buildSteps.detail: Use software to find a unique sequence near the gene's control region so the editor binds only there.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the epigenetic editor
buildSteps.detail: Fuse dCas9 to an effector enzyme — for example a methyltransferase to silence the gene, or an activator to boost it.

buildSteps.title: Add an environmental trigger
buildSteps.detail: Link the editor's production to a promoter that responds to a chosen cue, so the trait switches on only when needed.

buildSteps.title: Introduce into plant cells
buildSteps.detail: Deliver the DNA into callus tissue or protoplasts using Agrobacterium or a gene gun.

buildSteps.title: Regenerate and select
buildSteps.detail: Grow edited cells into whole plants under selection, then check that the epigenetic mark is present.

buildSteps.title: Test in greenhouse and field
buildSteps.detail: Confirm the trait appears only when the trigger is present and that the mark is stable across generations.

buildSteps.title: Remove the editing machinery
buildSteps.detail: If needed, cross out the transgenes so the final plant carries only the epigenetic change, not the editing tools.

prerequisites.why: provides a programmable way to reach a specific DNA sequence without cutting it.
shown in model plants like Arabidopsis, but few effectors have been tuned for major crops.
needed to turn edited cells into whole plants, though it remains difficult for some varieties.
some stress-responsive promoters are known, but precise, reversible control is still being developed.
for most agronomic traits we do not yet know which marks to change and where.

pathway.milestone: proof-of-concept in model species such as Arabidopsis, changing flowering time or stress response through targeted methylation
pathway.unlocks: confidence that epigenetic marks can be written at chosen sites in plants.

pathway.milestone: demonstration in major crops like rice, wheat or tomato under controlled conditions
pathway.unlocks: evidence that the approach can work in plants people actually eat.

pathway.milestone: field trials where a natural trigger such as drought switches the trait on
pathway.unlocks: real-world validation of the environmental switch.

pathway.milestone: regulatory approval and commercial varieties with stacked epigenetic traits
pathway.unlocks: climate-ready crops that adjust to weather without permanent genetic change.
